title: Design a Multi-Tenant Team Messaging Platform
prompt: Design workplace messaging with workspaces, channels, DMs, multi-device synchronization, notifications, files, and deletion. Handle both small conversations and very large channels. Cover authorization, durable ordering, reconnect, fan-out, search boundaries, and operational isolation.

response.placeholder: Choose an ordering scope and explain why a huge channel cannot use the same per-recipient fan-out as a DM.
response.reference_answer:
## Data and ordering
Every key includes workspace scope. Append messages to a durable per-conversation log with monotonically increasing sequence numbers, then maintain inbox/read projections. Validate membership and role permissions before the write.

## Fan-out and sync
DMs and small channels can materialize recipient inbox notifications. Large channels use a shared timeline plus gateway broadcast and read-time cursors, avoiding millions of durable copies. Devices reconnect with a conversation cursor and receive a snapshot/gap page; acknowledgement and notification operations are idempotent.

## Files and deletion
Store bytes separately with scoped upload credentials; metadata and ACLs reference immutable blobs. Deletion creates a tombstone reflected in timeline/search projections, with legal-retention policy explicit.

## Operations
Measure hot-channel fan-out, gateway lag, reconnect gap size, notification drops, tenant quotas, and authorization denials.

## Progressive Hints
1. There is no useful global message order.
2. Separate timeline storage from recipient views.
3. A tombstone is not immediately physical deletion.
